historical_references.reference:
Al-Salih Ayyub was a Sultan of the Ayyubid Empire, ruling from 1240 to 1249. He is known for his military victories against the Mongols and Crusaders.
Context: Al-Salih Ayyub was the son of Sultan Al-Kamil and served as a governor in Egypt and Syria under his father. When his father died in 1238, Al-Salih Ayyub succeeded him and faced numerous challenges from the Mongols and the Crusaders. Despite these challenges, he was able to maintain the territorial integrity of the Ayyubid Empire and even expanded it in some areas.

Salih al-Din Yusuf (Saladin) was a Kurdish Muslim ruler who founded the Ayyubid Empire in 1171. He is best known for his role in the Crusades and recapturing Jerusalem from the Crusaders.
Context: Salih al-Din Yusuf was a military leader under the vizier of Egypt, Shawar, and rose to power after Shawar's assassination. He gained control of Damascus in 1154 and went on to conquer Egypt and Syria, establishing the Ayyubid Empire in 1171. He is remembered for his military victories against the Crusaders, including the recapture of Jerusalem in 1187.
